fatal_errors: The proposed Q235 pre-oxidation treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention: an atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L followed by 2 h annealing, optimally at 550 °C.

The asserted protective magnetite/hematite mechanism is not supported by the cited evidence. E1 concerns oxidation resistance of an AlCrTiZrMo HEA film, while E2 discusses compact Cr-, Al-, or Si-rich oxides and their instability in molten fluoride salts, not protective iron oxides on Q235 in sulfate/chloride salts.

The room-temperature rationale is internally inconsistent: the same oxide is pre-formed at 700 °C before both exposures, so slower room-temperature oxide-growth kinetics cannot by itself explain why that pre-existing film would be less coalesced.

A thick iron-oxide scale produced by 10 h air annealing at 700 °C may be porous, layered, or poorly adherent and vulnerable to chloride/sulfate fluxing; its assumed density, adhesion, and self-healing are treated as premises rather than demonstrated mediators.
explanation: This is a testable alternative centered on pre-oxidation of Q235, with a reasonable untreated baseline, pre-exposure characterization, matched exposures, and an explicit falsification rule. It also overlaps broadly with the target in predicting that a continuous oxide barrier can lower mass change and localized attack during 900 °C Na2SO4/NaCl exposure. However, it misses the target material, HEA deposition, annealing-temperature series, 550 °C optimum, acidic electrochemical condition, Al/Cr-rich passive products, and comparisons against both uncoated and as-sprayed specimens. The evidence establishes only the general possibility of oxide-mediated protection and does not validate magnetite/hematite protection under the proposed conditions. A stronger study would include annealing-atmosphere controls, quantify pre-exposure scale mass separately, test scale adhesion and cross-sectional penetration, and compare pre-oxidized specimens with identically heat-treated specimens whose oxide was removed.
